from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

# Define the circuit with 4 qubits and 4 classical bits
qc = QuantumCircuit(4, 4)

# Step 1: Apply H gate to all qubits
qc.h(0)
qc.h(1)
qc.h(2)
qc.h(3)

# Step 2: Apply Rz gates
qc.rz(2.8507, 0)
qc.rz(0.2836, 1)
qc.rz(2.7925, 2)
qc.rz(2.7328, 3)

# Step 3: Apply CNOT(0,1), then Rz(1.6627) to qubit 1, then CNOT(0,1)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.rz(1.6627, 1)
qc.cx(0, 1)

# Step 4: Apply CNOT(1,2), then Rz(1.9952) to qubit 2, then CNOT(1,2)
qc.cx(1, 2)
qc.rz(1.9952, 2)
qc.cx(1, 2)

# Step 5: Apply CNOT(2,3), then Rz(0.2854) to qubit 3, then CNOT(2,3)
qc.cx(2, 3)
qc.rz(0.2854, 3)
qc.cx(2, 3)

# Step 6: Repeat Steps 1-5 exactly once more (second ZZ layer)
qc.h(0)
qc.h(1)
qc.h(2)
qc.h(3)

qc.rz(2.8507, 0)
qc.rz(0.2836, 1)
qc.rz(2.7925, 2)
qc.rz(2.7328, 3)

qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.rz(1.6627, 1)
qc.cx(0, 1)

qc.cx(1, 2)
qc.rz(1.9952, 2)
qc.cx(1, 2)

qc.cx(2, 3)
qc.rz(0.2854, 3)
qc.cx(2, 3)

# Step 7: Measure qubits 0,1,2,3
qc.measure([0, 1, 2, 3], [0, 1, 2, 3])

print(qc.draw())
